title: Purushottam Das Tandon
summary: Seconded the Objectives Resolution on 13 December; on 18 December argued that members and parties needed adequate time to study the Assembly Rules.

title: M. R. Masani
summary: Read the Objectives Resolution through democratic socialism, individual liberty and the long-term transformation of minorities into a common nation.

title: Frank Anthony
summary: Supported Dr. Jayakar’s amendment to defer parts of the declaration in the interest of wider agreement and participation.

title: Syama Prasad Mookerjee
summary: Opposed postponement and argued that the Assembly’s ultimate political sanction came from the people of India.

title: Sardar Ujjal Singh
summary: Supported the Resolution while placing Sikh minority safeguards, Punjab and opposition to partition squarely before the House.

title: Seth Govind Das
summary: Spoke in Hindustani, connected freedom with democratic-socialist aspiration and urged the Assembly to continue despite external obstruction.

title: Ananthasayanam Ayyangar
summary: Requested a full Christmas-week recess before the Assembly resumed in the new year.

title: Hriday Nath Kunzru
summary: Raised scheduling concerns and then defended postponement of the Objectives Resolution as a way to strengthen participation and the Assembly’s moral authority.

title: Dhirendra Nath Datta
summary: Asked for more time to scrutinise the Rules and later made a brief interjection during the debate on grouping.

title: J. J. M. Nichols-Roy
summary: Supported the Resolution, defended religious freedom and minority security, and argued that autonomous units could coexist with a democratic Indian Union.

title: Debi Prasad Khaitan
summary: Argued that Constituent Assembly work and completion of the Rules should take precedence over other engagements.

title: Mohan Lal Saksena
summary: Suggested rearranging sittings to give the Rules Committee more time and bring completed rules before the House sooner.

title: R. K. Sidhwa
summary: Defended adequate rule scrutiny and later rejected British minority propaganda, drawing on Parsi experience and opposition to separate electorates.

title: Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel
summary: Insisted that Constituent Assembly business take precedence and that the Rules be finished before the preliminary session dispersed.

title: K. Santhanam
summary: Proposed taking completed portions of the Rules before the Assembly rather than waiting for the entire draft.

title: Sri Biswanath Das
summary: Supported the Resolution, discussed grouping and popular sovereignty in the States, and rebutted claims that the Assembly was a caste-Hindu body.

title: N. Gopalaswami Ayyangar
summary: Opposed postponement, asserted broad constituent power and argued that real constitutional authority in Indian States must derive from their people.
